title: A hit can be stale
lesson: Recognize a stale runbook cache hit and trace explicit invalidation followed by a tool-managed source read and refill.
limitations: Illustrative serialized recovery; invalidation does not guarantee consistency under concurrent writes, stale fills or failed deletion.
Red highlighting shows the viewer a revision mismatch; the tool does not automatically detect stale data.
The editor and invalidation trigger are abstracted; the application layer owns deletion and refill.
TTL, permissions, outages and deployment execution are outside this cut; prompts do not enforce permissions.
Sound analyzed, not physically listened to; self-reviewed without a comparative recommendation.

transcript.text: The agent asks a read tool for a runbook. The tool finds revision 1 in the cache and returns it without reading the source. Both stored copies currently match.

An independent edit commits revision 2 to the source. The next request still gets revision 1 from the cache. Red highlighting reveals the mismatch to the viewer; it does not represent automatic freshness detection.
An explicit recovery action deletes the cached guide after the source edit. The cache entry becomes empty. The agent still holds its previously returned revision 1.
The next lookup misses. The tool reads revision 2 from the source, writes it into the cache, and returns it to the agent. This example assumes those operations succeed without concurrent writes.
A repeat request now uses cached revision 2. The matching revisions hold on screen before a fade to black. This demonstrates reuse after recovery, not a guarantee that future reads remain fresh.
